intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under hundreds of cherry blossom trees in Kyoto's most famous park. Spread a picnic blanket, enjoy traditional snacks, and soak in the magical pink canopy with your family. The iconic weeping cherry tree at the center is illuminated at night for a breathtaking effect.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Tokyo's legendary Tsukiji Outer Market and sample iconic Japanese street foods including fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), matcha soft serve, and grilled seafood skewers. A fantastic family-friendly culinary adventure that introduces everyone to authentic Japanese flavors in a vibrant, bustling atmosphere.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the iconic towering bamboo groves of Arashiyama, then hike up to the Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids and adults alike will love feeding the monkeys while enjoying panoramic views of Kyoto below. Combine with a rickshaw ride for extra fun.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a world-class interactive digital art experience at teamLab Borderless, one of the most visited museums in the world. Walk through rooms filled with infinite light installations, interactive projections, and mesmerizing digital waterfalls. A mind-blowing blend of technology, art, and culture that captivates all ages.

experiences.name: Nara Deer Park and Todai-ji Temple Visit
experiences.description: Take a day trip to Nara to hand-feed over 1,200 freely roaming sacred deer, then visit the awe-inspiring Todai-ji Temple housing Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue. This UNESCO World Heritage site offers a perfect blend of wildlife interaction, ancient culture, and history that the whole family will treasure.
experiences.location: Nara Park, Nara City, Nara Prefecture

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at 13:00, clear customs and immigration, collect luggage. Take the budget-friendly airport limousine bus or train to your hotel (Aegean Bliss Resort, Beachfront area). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the nearby beachfront promenade to get oriented. Enjoy the coastal scenery and spot any early cherry blossom trees in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the immediate neighborhood around the hotel. Visit a nearby convenience store (7-Eleven, FamilyMart, or Lawson) to stock up on affordable snacks and drinks. Enjoy a relaxed first dinner close to the hotel and get an early night to recover from the flight.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or skip — arrive at 13:00
meals.lunch: Convenience store bento box or onigiri (rice balls) near the airport or train station — approx ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Local ramen shop or family restaurant (Gusto, Saizeriya) near the hotel — approx ¥700–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Japan's IC transit cards (Suica or Pasmo) can be loaded at the airport and save money on trains and buses throughout the trip. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local park or seaside garden known for cherry blossoms. Bring a convenience store picnic breakfast and enjoy hanami (flower viewing) under the blooming sakura trees. Mid-April is peak or late cherry blossom season in many parts of Japan — a perfect and free cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby traditional shrine or temple for a cultural immersion. Many shrines are free to enter. Purchase an omamori (lucky charm) as a souvenir (approx ¥500). Explore the shrine grounds, take photos, and learn about Shinto traditions. Walk through any local shopping arcade (shotengai) nearby for budget souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beachfront area for a sunset walk. Enjoy the coastal atmosphere and look for a local izakaya (Japanese pub) for an affordable dinner with small shared plates.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store onigiri, tamagoyaki egg, and canned coffee — approx ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Picnic under the cherry blossoms: convenience store sandwiches, fruit, and tea — approx ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Local izakaya — yakitori skewers, edamame, and miso soup — approx ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: April 2027 cherry blossoms may be at late bloom stage — check local bloom forecast apps like Sakura Navi. Bring a picnic mat for hanami.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget local train or bus to the nearest major city center. Visit a famous historic district or old town area with preserved traditional architecture. Many such areas are free to walk through. Look for machiya (traditional townhouses) and local craft shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a free or low-cost public museum or cultural center. Many Japanese prefectural museums offer free or discounted entry (¥200–¥500). Look for exhibits on local history, samurai culture, or traditional arts. Families can enjoy interactive displays.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a local covered shopping arcade and try street food snacks such as takoyaki (octopus balls), taiyaki (fish-shaped cake), or crepes. Great for families and very budget-friendly.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or convenience store — approx ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Teishoku (set meal) at a local diner — rice, miso soup, and main dish — approx ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Street food in the shopping arcade — takoyaki, taiyaki, and drinks — approx ¥600–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Use IC card on local trains for seamless and discounted travel. Many museums are closed on Mondays — check opening days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a traditional Japanese garden (Japanese gardens often charge a small entry fee of ¥200–¥500). Appreciate the carefully manicured landscapes, koi ponds, and any remaining cherry blossoms. Great for family photos and a peaceful cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a local hands-on cultural workshop such as origami, calligraphy, or pottery. Many community centers and tourist spots offer budget workshops for ¥500–¥1,500 per person. A wonderful family activity that doubles as a cultural souvenir.
day_by_day.evening: Cook-your-own dinner experience at a budget yakiniku (grilled meat) restaurant. Many offer affordable lunch-priced sets in the evening or early bird specials. Fun and interactive for families.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store toast, yogurt, and juice — approx ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Soba noodle restaurant near the garden — cold or hot soba with tempura — approx ¥700–¥1,100
meals.dinner: Budget yakiniku or Korean BBQ restaurant — approx ¥1,200–¥1,800 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book cultural workshops in advance if possible, especially for families. Many tourist information centers (kanko annai) can help arrange local activities for free.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip: Take an early train to a nearby famous cherry blossom spot or castle town. Japan's regional castles (such as those in Himeji, Matsuyama, or Hikone depending on your region) are iconic and family-friendly. Castle entry is typically ¥300–¥800 per adult.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the castle grounds and surrounding moat area, often lined with cherry blossom trees. Pack a convenience store lunch to eat in the castle park — a classic Japanese experience. Visit any free samurai district or historic walking path nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel by early evening. Stop at a local supermarket (depachika basement food hall or grocery store) to pick up discounted bento boxes and side dishes for a budget hotel-room dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before catching the train — approx ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Convenience store picnic at the castle park — approx ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Supermarket discounted bento and side dishes (often 20–30% off after 7 PM) — approx ¥600–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Check train schedules in advance. Japan's regional trains can be infrequent — plan return times carefully. IC cards work on most regional lines.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the local fish market or morning market near the beachfront hotel. Many coastal towns in Japan have lively morning markets with fresh seafood, produce, and local snacks. Free to browse and very culturally immersive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local aquarium or marine-themed attraction — great for families. Many regional aquariums offer family ticket discounts (approx ¥1,500–¥2,500 for adults, less for children). Alternatively, enjoy free beach activities and beachcombing along the hotel's coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a seafood dinner at a local kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) restaurant. Budget-friendly and a quintessential Japanese family dining experience — plates start from ¥110–¥165 each.

meals.breakfast: Fresh snacks from the morning market — grilled seafood, tamagoyaki, or local pastries — approx ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Simple udon at a local udon chain (Marugame Seimen or similar) — approx ¥400–¥700
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) — approx ¥1,000–¥1,800 per person

day_by_day.notes: Morning markets typically run from 6–10 AM. Arrive early for the best selection. Kaiten-zushi restaurants are very child-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a famous local Shinto shrine or Buddhist temple complex. Many are free or charge minimal entry. Participate in the morning ritual atmosphere — monks chanting, incense burning, and worshippers making offerings. A deeply cultural and memorable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local craft or antique market if one is scheduled (many Japanese towns hold weekend markets). Browse handmade goods, vintage items, and local art. Great for unique budget souvenirs. Alternatively, visit a 100-yen shop (Daiso or Seria) for affordable Japanese goods and gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Try a public onsen (hot spring bath) experience at a local sento (public bathhouse). Entry is typically ¥400–¥800 per person — an authentic and relaxing Japanese cultural tradition perfect for families.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store — approx ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Curry rice at a budget Japanese curry chain (CoCo Ichibanya) — approx ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) set meal at a local restaurant — approx ¥900–¥1,400

day_by_day.notes: Onsen etiquette: tattoos may be restricted at some facilities. Bring a small towel or rent one on-site. Children are welcome at most sento.

day_by_day.morning: Take a scenic nature hike or coastal walk. Japan's coastlines and countryside offer beautiful free walking trails. Look for signposted nature paths near the hotel. Enjoy spring wildflowers, ocean views, and fresh air — ideal for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local folk museum or open-air heritage village (minka-en). These living history museums preserve traditional farmhouses and crafts. Entry is typically ¥300–¥600. Children love exploring the old buildings and hands-on demonstrations.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost local community event, festival, or evening market if available in April. Many Japanese towns hold spring matsuri (festivals) in April. Check local tourism boards for events. Enjoy festival food stalls.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store — onigiri, hard-boiled eggs, and green tea — approx ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from convenience store eaten on the trail — approx ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Festival food stalls (yakisoba, corn on the cob, kakigori) or local gyoza restaurant — approx ¥700–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the hike. Check local event calendars at the tourist information center or via Japan's tourism website.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — revisit your favorite cherry blossom spot for one last hanami picnic. Take family photos and soak in the peaceful beauty of Japan's most iconic spring tradition. Buy any last-minute snacks and drinks from a convenience store.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shopping for souvenirs at a budget-friendly location: 100-yen shops, local craft stores, or temple souvenir stalls. Great picks include matcha sweets, tenugui (hand towels), chopsticks, and small ceramics — all very affordable. Visit any missed local attraction.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special but still budget-friendly restaurant. Try shabu-shabu (hot pot) at a lunch-priced evening restaurant or visit a local specialty restaurant for a regional dish you haven't tried yet. Celebrate a wonderful trip to Japan.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a sit-down kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) breakfast set — approx ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Hanami picnic under the cherry blossoms — convenience store or bakery spread — approx ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a local specialty restaurant — approx ¥1,200–¥2,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep receipts for tax-free shopping (purchases over ¥5,000 at participating stores qualify for tourist tax refunds). Pack souvenirs carefully to avoid excess baggage fees.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a slow breakfast and pack remaining luggage. Take one last walk along the beachfront to say goodbye to the ocean view. Check out of the hotel and store luggage if needed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, visit any last nearby attraction or simply relax at a local café with a matcha latte. Head to the airport or train station with plenty of time. Use IC card for transit to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Browse airport shops for any final omiyage (gift) purchases — airport duty-free shops often stock the same popular Japanese snacks and sweets. Board your flight home with wonderful memories of Japan.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store — approx ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or terminal food court — ramen, soba, or bento — approx ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Meal on the plane or airport departure lounge

day_by_day.notes: Return your IC card at the airport for a refund of the remaining balance (minus a small handling fee). Arrive at the airport at least 2–3 hours before international departure. Double-check passport, tickets, and all belongings before leaving the hotel.

trip_options.title: Classic Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Narita/Haneda Express or airport limousine bus to your accommodation (Aegean Bliss Resort). Journey takes approximately 60–90 minutes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hotel Check-In & Neighborhood Orientation — Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll around the beachfront resort area. Get acquainted with nearby convenience stores (7-Eleven, Lawson) for snacks and essentials. Pick up a Suica/Pasmo IC card at the nearest train station for seamless travel throughout the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Easy First Night Dinner — Head to a nearby family-friendly izakaya or ramen shop within walking distance of the hotel. Keep it low-key to recover from jet lag. Return early for a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab onigiri and green tea from an airport convenience store upon landing.
meals.lunch: Airport ramen or soba at a terminal restaurant (budget ¥1,000–¥1,500) before or after immigration.
meals.dinner: Local izakaya near the resort — try yakitori skewers, miso soup, and rice sets (budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag is real — prioritize rest tonight. Set alarms to wake at a normal local time. April 15 is prime cherry blossom season, so expect crowds at popular spots throughout the trip. Book any reserved experiences in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Head to Tsukiji Outer Market early (open from 5:00 AM, best visited 8:00–10:00 AM). Sample iconic Japanese street foods: fresh tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), tuna sashimi, grilled scallops, and matcha soft-serve. Wander the stalls and soak in the vibrant atmosphere of one of Tokyo's most beloved food destinations.
day_by_day.afternoon: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum — Take the subway to teamLab Borderless (check current location post-2024 reopening in Azabudai Hills). Spend 2–3 hours immersing the whole family in breathtaking interactive digital art installations. Kids and adults alike will be amazed by the borderless, room-filling light and sound experiences. Book tickets online in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Odaiba Waterfront Stroll & Dinner — Since teamLab is near the waterfront district, enjoy a sunset walk along Tokyo Bay with views of the Rainbow Bridge. Dine at DiverCity Tokyo Plaza or a nearby mall food court with diverse family-friendly options.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light bite at the hotel before heading out — coffee and toast.
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Outer Market stall hopping — fresh sushi, grilled seafood skewers, tamagoyaki (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 total grazing).
meals.dinner: Odaiba dining — try a conveyor-belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) restaurant like Sushiro or a ramen chain (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person).

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless tickets sell out — book online at least 1–2 weeks ahead. Wear comfortable shoes for Tsukiji. The market is best enjoyed on a weekday morning. Bring cash as some stalls are cash-only.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Kyoto via Shinkansen — Take the bullet train from Tokyo Station (approximately 2 hours 15 minutes on the Nozomi/Hikari). Arrive in Kyoto mid-morning. Drop bags at a coin locker at Kyoto Station and head straight to Maruyama Park for cherry blossom viewing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park — Experience hanami (flower viewing) under hundreds of magnificent cherry blossom trees in Kyoto's most beloved park. The iconic weeping cherry tree at the center is spectacular in full bloom. Walk through neighboring Yasaka Shrine, explore the charming Gion district streets, and take photos in the historic stone-paved Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka lanes.
day_by_day.evening: Gion District & Traditional Kaiseki Dinner — As dusk falls, stroll through Gion hoping to spot a maiko (apprentice geisha). Enjoy a mid-range kaiseki (multi-course Japanese dinner) at a local Kyoto restaurant, featuring seasonal spring ingredients. Check into your Kyoto accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick convenience store onigiri before catching the Shinkansen.
meals.lunch: Bento box purchased at Tokyo Station's Gransta food hall to enjoy on the bullet train (budget ¥1,000–¥1,500).
meals.dinner: Kyoto kaiseki set menu at a local restaurant in Gion — look for fixed-price lunch/dinner sets (budget ¥3,000–¥5,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book Shinkansen tickets in advance via the JR Pass or online reservation. April weekends in Kyoto are extremely crowded — arrive at Maruyama Park early afternoon to secure a good spot. The weeping cherry tree is illuminated at night — beautiful for evening photos.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove — Take a bus or train to Arashiyama and walk through the iconic towering bamboo groves. Arrive before 9:00 AM to beat the crowds. The rustling bamboo and filtered morning light create an otherworldly atmosphere. Visit the nearby Tenryu-ji Temple and its stunning moss garden (UNESCO World Heritage Site).
day_by_day.afternoon: Iwatayama Monkey Park — After the bamboo grove, hike up the hill to the Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids will love hand-feeding the monkeys through a fence at the summit, which also offers a panoramic view over Kyoto city. Descend and explore Arashiyama's charming riverside shops and tofu restaurants.
day_by_day.evening: Arashiyama Rickshaw Ride & Riverside Dinner — Treat the family to a short rickshaw (jinrikisha) ride through scenic Arashiyama streets as the sun sets. Enjoy dinner at a riverside restaurant overlooking the Oi River — tofu cuisine (yudofu) is a Kyoto specialty perfect for this area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) near your accommodation.
meals.lunch: Arashiyama area — try a tofu set lunch or matcha-themed café along the bamboo grove path (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500).
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant in Arashiyama — yudofu (hot tofu) set dinner or kaiseki-lite (budget ¥2,500–¥4,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Monkey Park entry fee is ¥550 for adults, ¥250 for children. Do not bring food in open hands near the monkeys. The hike to the park takes about 20 minutes and involves some steep sections — wear good shoes. Rickshaw rides are a splurge but memorable (budget ¥3,000–¥8,000 depending on route).

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha — Rise early and visit Fushimi Inari Shrine before the crowds arrive. Walk through thousands of iconic vermilion torii gates winding up the forested mountain. Even a 30-minute hike partway up rewards with incredible photo opportunities and a sense of spiritual tranquility. The full hike to the summit takes about 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nishiki Market & Central Kyoto — Take the subway to central Kyoto and explore Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') — a narrow covered shopping street packed with vendors selling pickled vegetables, fresh tofu, street snacks, and local delicacies. Browse nearby Teramachi shopping arcade and visit Nijo Castle (UNESCO site) for a taste of feudal Japan.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Machiya (Townhouse) Neighborhood Walk & Dinner — Wander the preserved wooden machiya townhouses of the Nakagyo or Shimogyo districts as evening falls. Choose a cozy local restaurant for dinner — Kyoto-style obanzai (small vegetable and tofu dishes) is highly recommended.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before heading to Fushimi Inari (open 24 hours, best before 8 AM).
meals.lunch: Nishiki Market grazing — try dashimaki tamago, pickles, skewered tofu, and fresh mochi (budget ¥1,500–¥2,000 total).
meals.dinner: Obanzai restaurant in central Kyoto — a set meal with 6–8 small seasonal dishes (budget ¥2,500–¥3,500 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free to enter and open 24/7 — early morning is magical. Nijo Castle closes on Tuesdays, so Monday is ideal. Keep Nishiki Market snacks light as there are many tempting options — pace yourself!

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Nara — Take the JR Nara Line or Kintetsu train from Kyoto (45 minutes). Head straight to Nara Deer Park where over 1,200 freely roaming sacred deer greet visitors. Purchase shika senbei (deer crackers) from park vendors and hand-feed the gentle, bowing deer. A magical and unforgettable family experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Todai-ji Temple & Kasuga Taisha Shrine — Walk through the park to the awe-inspiring Todai-ji Temple, home to the Great Buddha (Daibutsu) — the world's largest bronze Buddha statue housed in the world's largest wooden building. Explore the temple grounds, then stroll to the vermilion Kasuga Taisha Shrine surrounded by hanging stone lanterns and deer.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto & Cherry Blossom Night Viewing — Return to Kyoto by early evening. Visit a cherry blossom illumination event (yozakura) — Maruyama Park and Heian Shrine often hold night-lit hanami events in April. Enjoy the magical pink blossoms glowing under lantern light.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or onigiri from a convenience store before the train.
meals.lunch: Nara town near the park — try kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi), a Nara specialty, at a local restaurant (budget ¥1,200–¥2,000).
meals.dinner: Kyoto station area after returning — Kyoto Ramen Koji (ramen alley on the 10th floor of Kyoto Station building) offers excellent variety (budget ¥1,000–¥1,500).

day_by_day.notes: Todai-ji entry is ¥600 for adults. Deer in Nara are wild — supervise young children and keep bags secure. The deer bow to ask for crackers! Nara is easily done as a day trip from Kyoto. Check illumination event schedules for Kyoto parks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Philosopher's Path & Silver Pavilion (Ginkaku-ji) — Walk the famous Philosopher's Path, a 2 km stone walkway along a cherry blossom-lined canal in northern Kyoto. In April, this is one of the most romantic and picturesque walks in all of Japan. End the walk at Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion) — a serene Zen temple with a raked sand garden and moss-covered grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Heian Shrine & Okazaki Area — Visit the grand Heian Shrine with its famous garden and large torii gate. The shrine's inner garden (Shin-en) features cherry blossoms reflected in ponds — a stunning April scene. Explore the Okazaki cultural district nearby, home to the Kyoto Municipal Museum of Art and a relaxed café scene.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to Osaka — Take the Hankyu or JR train to Osaka (30–40 minutes). Check into your Osaka accommodation. Explore the dazzling Dotonbori entertainment district at night — neon lights, giant mechanical crabs, and the energy of Japan's most exuberant city.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast along the Philosopher's Path — several charming cafés open from 8:00 AM.
meals.lunch: Okazaki area café or a bento from a department store basement (depachika) near Heian Shrine (budget ¥1,000–¥1,800).
meals.dinner: Dotonbori, Osaka — try takoyaki (octopus balls) and okonomiyaki (savory pancake) from street stalls and local restaurants. Osaka is famous for 'kuidaore' (eat until you drop) (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500).

day_by_day.notes: Ginkaku-ji entry is ¥500. Heian Shrine garden is ¥600. The Philosopher's Path is best walked northward (Nanzen-ji to Ginkaku-ji direction). Store luggage at Kyoto Station and collect it before heading to Osaka, or arrange hotel luggage forwarding (takkyubin service).

day_by_day.morning: Osaka Castle & Cherry Blossoms — Visit the magnificent Osaka Castle, one of Japan's most iconic landmarks. The castle park surrounding it is a top cherry blossom spot — stroll under the blossoms and visit the castle museum to learn about Japan's feudal history. The castle tower offers panoramic city views from the top floor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kuromon Ichiba Market & Shinsekai District — Explore Kuromon Ichiba ('Osaka's Kitchen'), a lively covered market with fresh seafood, wagyu beef skewers, and local snacks. Then head to the retro Shinsekai district, a nostalgic neighborhood with vintage architecture, kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) restaurants, and the Tsutenkaku Tower.
day_by_day.evening: Umeda Sky Building & Floating Garden Observatory — Take the subway to Umeda and visit the dramatic Floating Garden Observatory at the top of the Umeda Sky Building for spectacular 360-degree views of Osaka at night. Return to Dotonbori for a final evening stroll and dessert.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a Japanese morning set (morning setto) at a local kissaten café.
meals.lunch: Kuromon Market grazing — fresh uni (sea urchin), grilled scallops, and wagyu skewers (budget ¥2,000–¥3,000).
meals.dinner: Shinsekai kushikatsu restaurant — deep-fried skewers of meat, vegetables, and seafood dipped in a tangy sauce. A true Osaka tradition (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Osaka Castle museum entry is ¥600. Umeda Sky Building observatory is ¥1,500. The double-dipping rule in kushikatsu restaurants is strictly enforced — use the communal sauce only once per skewer! Osaka's food culture is legendary — embrace it fully.

day_by_day.morning: Universal Studios Japan (USJ) — Spend the morning at USJ, one of Japan's top family attractions. Highlights include The Wizarding World of Harry Potter, Super Nintendo World (book entry timed tickets in advance), and Minion Park. Arrive at park opening (usually 9:00 AM) to maximize time before crowds peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at Universal Studios Japan — Enjoy afternoon rides, shows, and character meet-and-greets. Super Nintendo World is particularly spectacular — families can interact with Mario-themed games throughout the land using Power-Up Bands (available for purchase inside). Grab park snacks like Butterbeer and Nintendo-themed treats.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Osaka & Farewell Osaka Dinner — Return to central Osaka by early evening. Enjoy a special family dinner in the Namba or Shinsaibashi area — try a teppanyaki restaurant where a chef cooks wagyu beef, seafood, and vegetables on a hot iron plate in front of you. A memorable and interactive dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast to fuel up before USJ.
meals.lunch: Inside USJ — Three Broomsticks in the Wizarding World for a Hogwarts-themed meal, or park food stalls (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 inside the park).
meals.dinner: Teppanyaki restaurant in Namba — mid-range set menus available (budget ¥4,000–¥6,000 per person for a special occasion dinner).

day_by_day.notes: USJ entry tickets must be purchased in advance online — they often sell out, especially during spring. Super Nintendo World requires a separate timed entry ticket (Area Timed Entry). Power-Up Bands are optional but enhance the experience (¥3,500 each). Arrive early to minimize wait times.

day_by_day.morning: Shinsaibashi Shopping & Last-Minute Souvenirs — Spend the morning exploring Shinsaibashi-suji shopping arcade and the adjacent Amerika-Mura district. Pick up last-minute souvenirs: matcha KitKats, wagashi (Japanese sweets), furoshiki wrapping cloths, and character goods. Visit a Don Quijote store for an eclectic range of affordable gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine — Visit one of Japan's oldest Shinto shrines, Sumiyoshi Taisha, which predates most other famous shrines and has a unique architectural style (sumiyoshi-zukuri) not found elsewhere. The grounds are peaceful and photogenic, with an arched drum bridge over a reflective pond — a tranquil final cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return Journey Preparation & Farewell Dinner — Return to your resort/hotel area. Enjoy a relaxed farewell dinner at a restaurant of your choice — perhaps revisiting a favorite dish from the trip (sushi, ramen, or tempura). Pack luggage, confirm return flight details, and reflect on 10 incredible days in Japan.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy it slowly on this final full day.
meals.lunch: Shinsaibashi area — try a conveyor-belt sushi restaurant like Hamazushi or Kura Sushi for a fun, affordable final sushi experience (budget ¥1,500–¥2,500).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — a mid-range tempura restaurant or sushi bar near your hotel. Splurge slightly on a quality meal to end the trip on a high note (budget ¥3,000–¥5,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Sumiyoshi Taisha is free to enter. Allow extra time at Shinsaibashi as it can get very crowded on Saturdays. If flying home the next day, confirm airport transfer arrangements the night before. Consider using a luggage forwarding service (takkyubin) to send bags directly to the airport the morning of departure for a stress-free journey.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under hundreds of cherry blossom trees in Kyoto's most famous park. Spread a picnic blanket, enjoy traditional snacks, and soak in the magical pink canopy with your family. The iconic weeping cherry tree at the center is illuminated at night for a breathtaking effect.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Tokyo's legendary Tsukiji Outer Market and sample iconic Japanese street foods including fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), matcha soft serve, and grilled seafood skewers. A fantastic family-friendly culinary adventure that introduces everyone to authentic Japanese flavors in a vibrant, bustling atmosphere.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the iconic towering bamboo groves of Arashiyama, then hike up to the Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids and adults alike will love feeding the monkeys while enjoying panoramic views of Kyoto below. Combine with a rickshaw ride for extra fun.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a world-class interactive digital art experience at teamLab Borderless, one of the most visited museums in the world. Walk through rooms filled with infinite light installations, interactive projections, and mesmerizing digital waterfalls. A mind-blowing blend of technology, art, and culture that captivates all ages.

experiences.name: Nara Deer Park and Todai-ji Temple Visit
experiences.description: Take a day trip to Nara to hand-feed over 1,200 freely roaming sacred deer, then visit the awe-inspiring Todai-ji Temple housing Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue. This UNESCO World Heritage site offers a perfect blend of wildlife interaction, ancient culture, and history that the whole family will treasure.
experiences.location: Nara Park, Nara City, Nara Prefecture

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and freshen up after landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, settle into your beachfront suite, and enjoy a welcome amenity with matcha tea and wagashi sweets prepared by the resort. Take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to decompress from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Orientation dinner at the resort's signature restaurant. Enjoy a curated kaiseki-inspired welcome menu featuring seasonal ingredients, paired with premium sake selections. Early night to recover from jet lag.

meals.breakfast: Onboard or at airport lounge
meals.lunch: Light bento or ramen at airport arrival hall (Narita/Haneda premium food court)
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — multi-course kaiseki welcome dinner with sake pairing (¥20,000–¥30,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private luxury transfer (black car or limousine service) from the airport in advance. Confirm resort check-in time and request early luggage storage if needed. Allow time to adjust to Japan Standard Time (UTC+9).

day_by_day.morning: Begin the day with a premium Japanese breakfast at the resort featuring grilled fish, miso soup, tamagoyaki, and seasonal pickles. Then head to teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum for a world-class immersive digital art experience — an unforgettable activity for the whole family. Book a private early-access slot for a crowd-free experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After teamLab, explore the nearby Odaiba waterfront area. Visit the iconic Rainbow Bridge viewpoint and browse the upscale DiverCity Tokyo Plaza. Enjoy a relaxed seaside walk and let the kids experience the futuristic atmosphere of this man-made island.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a renowned teppanyaki restaurant in Odaiba or back near the resort. Watch expert chefs prepare premium Wagyu beef, lobster, and seasonal vegetables on an iron griddle right at your table — theatrical and delicious.

meals.breakfast: Resort Japanese breakfast set — grilled fish, rice, miso soup, pickles, tamagoyaki (included or ¥5,000 per person)
meals.lunch: Bills Odaiba or Tableaux — upscale international brunch/lunch with harbor views (¥4,000–¥8,000 per person)
meals.dinner: Teppanyaki Mihara or Ukai-tei Odaiba — premium Wagyu teppanyaki dinner (¥25,000–¥40,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab Borderless tickets well in advance as they sell out quickly. Request a private or semi-private teppanyaki table for a more exclusive family experience. Comfortable walking shoes recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour. Arrive early to experience the vibrant market atmosphere at its freshest. Sample iconic Japanese street foods including fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, and matcha-flavored treats. A private guide will curate the best stalls and explain the cultural significance of each delicacy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll to the nearby Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning traditional Japanese garden with a teahouse set against the Tokyo skyline. Enjoy an authentic matcha tea ceremony experience in the garden's historic teahouse overlooking the tidal pond. Afterward, take a scenic water bus along the Sumida River.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sushi Saito or a similarly prestigious Michelin-starred sushi counter in Tokyo. Experience omakase dining at its finest — the chef selects the finest seasonal ingredients and crafts each piece with extraordinary precision.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or light pastries and coffee before the market tour
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Outer Market tasting tour — curated premium street food experience (¥5,000–¥10,000 per person with guide)
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred omakase sushi counter (Sushi Yoshitake, Sushi Sho, or equivalent) — ¥40,000–¥60,000 per person; reserve months in advance

day_by_day.notes: The Tsukiji market is best visited before 10:00 AM for the freshest experience — arrange an early departure from the resort. The matcha ceremony at Hamarikyu costs approximately ¥500 per person and is walk-in friendly. Omakase reservations require advance booking; concierge assistance is highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Private shinkansen (bullet train) transfer to Kyoto — a thrilling and iconic Japanese experience in itself. Board the Nozomi from Tokyo Station in Green Car (first class) for a smooth 2h15m journey with Mt. Fuji views on a clear day. Arrive in Kyoto and check luggage into a luxury ryokan or hotel for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head directly to Maruyama Park for the Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami) experience. Stroll beneath hundreds of blossoming sakura trees in Kyoto's most celebrated park. A private guide will lead you through the park and surrounding Higashiyama district, including a visit to Yasaka Shrine draped in pink blossoms.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional kaiseki dinner at a renowned Kyoto ryotei (high-end traditional restaurant). Dine in a private tatami room with a garden view, experiencing the pinnacle of Japanese culinary artistry with 10–12 seasonal courses.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure or premium ekiben (station bento) from Tokyo Station's Gransta food hall
meals.lunch: Kyoto Nishiki Market light lunch — yudofu (tofu hot pot), pickles, and matcha sweets near Gion (¥3,000–¥6,000)
meals.dinner: Kikunoi Honten or Nakamura — Michelin-starred kaiseki ryotei in Kyoto (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Green Car shinkansen tickets in advance via JR Pass or direct purchase. Cherry blossoms in mid-April may be at late bloom or petal-fall stage ('hanafubuki') — still breathtakingly beautiful. Evening in Maruyama Park with lantern-lit blossoms is magical; consider staying after dinner for a night hanami walk.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Arashiyama Bamboo Grove. Walk through the iconic towering bamboo forest at dawn before the crowds arrive, accompanied by a knowledgeable guide who shares the cultural and historical significance of the area. Visit Tenryu-ji Temple's UNESCO World Heritage garden, one of Japan's most celebrated Zen gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up to the Iwatayama Monkey Park for a unique family experience — over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely on the mountaintop with panoramic views of Kyoto below. Afterward, explore Arashiyama's charming riverside streets, visiting artisan shops and the elegant Okochi Sanso villa garden.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Kyoto. Evening stroll through the atmospheric Gion district, Japan's most famous geisha quarter. With luck, spot a geisha or maiko hurrying to an appointment along Hanamikoji Street. Dinner at a celebrated Gion restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Ryokan or hotel Japanese breakfast — or a premium café near Arashiyama
meals.lunch: Shigetsu vegetarian shojin ryori (Buddhist cuisine) at Tenryu-ji — a unique and refined dining experience (¥5,000–¥8,000 per person)
meals.dinner: Gion Nanba or Mizai — intimate Kyoto cuisine in the heart of Gion (¥25,000–¥45,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Arashiyama Bamboo Grove before 8:00 AM for the most serene experience. The Monkey Park involves a 20-minute uphill hike — comfortable shoes essential. Children typically love the monkey park. Consider arranging a private rickshaw (jinrikisha) ride through Arashiyama for a premium touch.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara by private car or direct train (45 minutes from Kyoto). Visit Nara Deer Park and hand-feed over 1,200 freely roaming sacred sika deer — an extraordinary family experience. The deer are considered divine messengers and wander freely through the park and streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the awe-inspiring Todai-ji Temple, home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue (Daibutsu) standing 15 meters tall. Explore the surrounding Nara Park grounds, including Kasuga Taisha Grand Shrine with its thousands of stone and bronze lanterns lining forest paths. Browse Naramachi, the preserved merchant district, for artisan crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by private car. Enjoy a relaxing onsen (hot spring bath) experience at your ryokan or a premium public bathhouse. Dinner at a renowned Kyoto restaurant specializing in Kyoto-style cuisine (Kyo-ryori).

meals.breakfast: Hotel or ryokan breakfast in Kyoto before departure
meals.lunch: Edosan or Yanagichaya in Nara — traditional Japanese lunch near Todai-ji with garden views (¥5,000–¥10,000 per person)
meals.dinner: Hyotei or Nakamura Tokichi — iconic Kyoto cuisine dinner (¥25,000–¥40,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase deer crackers (shika senbei, ¥200) from park vendors to feed the deer — they can be surprisingly assertive! Children should be supervised around the deer. Todai-ji charges a small admission fee. Private car hire for Nara is recommended for maximum flexibility and comfort.

day_by_day.morning: Private tea ceremony and ikebana (flower arranging) workshop at a traditional Kyoto machiya townhouse. A master tea practitioner guides the family through the philosophy and ritual of chado (the way of tea), followed by a hands-on ikebana session — a deeply cultural and meditative morning experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine — thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up a forested mountainside. Hike the lower trail for spectacular photo opportunities without the full 2–3 hour summit hike. Afterward, visit the nearby Fushimi sake district for a premium sake tasting at a historic brewery.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Kyoto at a top-tier restaurant. Consider a private dinner in a traditional kyo-machiya townhouse with a personal chef preparing a multi-course meal — an exclusive and intimate culinary experience.

meals.breakfast: Ryokan or hotel Japanese breakfast
meals.lunch: Tofuya Ukai near Fushimi — elegant tofu cuisine in a beautiful traditional setting (¥8,000–¥15,000 per person)
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner in a machiya townhouse or Mizai / The Westin Miyako Kyoto's fine dining (¥35,000–¥60,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the tea ceremony and ikebana workshop in advance through a cultural experience specialist or hotel concierge. Fushimi Inari is free to enter and most atmospheric at dawn or dusk — the afternoon light through the torii gates is dramatic. Sake tasting at Gekkeikan Okura Sake Museum is a refined cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private shinkansen or luxury coach transfer back to Tokyo. Arrive mid-morning and check back into the resort. Freshen up and enjoy a light lunch at the resort before heading out. Alternatively, take a scenic detour via Hakone for Mt. Fuji views en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Meiji Jingu Shrine in Harajuku — Tokyo's most serene and majestic Shinto shrine set within a 70-hectare forested sanctuary. Walk the grand gravel path through towering cedar trees to the main shrine. Afterward, explore the upscale Omotesando Avenue — Tokyo's Champs-Élysées — for world-class boutique shopping and architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop cocktails at a Tokyo sky bar (Park Hyatt Tokyo's New York Bar or Andaz Tokyo's rooftop) with panoramic city views. Dinner at a celebrated Tokyo restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or ryokan breakfast in Kyoto before departure
meals.lunch: Resort lunch or Omotesando Hills café — light and elegant (¥3,000–¥6,000)
meals.dinner: Quintessence or L'Effervescence — Tokyo's finest French-Japanese fusion, Michelin 3-star (¥35,000–¥55,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Meiji Shrine is free to visit and most peaceful on weekday mornings. Omotesando is ideal for premium shopping — Issey Miyake, Comme des Garçons, and flagship international brands line the boulevard. Reserve sky bar tables in advance for guaranteed sunset views.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided cultural immersion morning: visit the historic Yanaka district — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old neighborhoods with traditional shotengai (shopping streets), Buddhist temples, and artisan workshops. Explore at a leisurely pace with a local historian guide who brings Edo-period Tokyo to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon at leisure for family relaxation at the resort's beachfront facilities — pool, spa treatments, or beach activities. Alternatively, visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum for an immersive journey through the city's history from the Edo period to modern times — highly educational and entertaining for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell dinner experience — reserve a private dining room at one of Tokyo's most celebrated restaurants, or book an exclusive chef's table experience. Toast to an extraordinary journey through Japan.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full Japanese or Western set
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza shotengai — artisan street food and local specialties (¥2,000–¥4,000 per person)
meals.dinner: Sukiyabashi Jiro Roppongi or Saito — legendary sushi or premium Japanese farewell dinner (¥40,000–¥70,000 per person; reserve well in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is a wonderful contrast to modern Tokyo and beloved by families and culture enthusiasts alike. The Edo-Tokyo Museum (Ryogoku) is approximately 30 minutes from the resort — check opening hours in advance. Begin packing and organize any tax-free shopping receipts for airport refund processing.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Japan — enjoy a leisurely premium breakfast at the resort. Take a last sunrise walk along the beachfront. Visit the resort spa for a rejuvenating treatment or simply relax by the ocean. Complete any final souvenir shopping at the resort boutique or nearby shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer to Narita or Haneda Airport. Arrive with ample time for tax-free refund processing, duty-free shopping, and a final Japanese meal at the airport's premium restaurant level.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry warm memories, artisan souvenirs, and the flavors of Japan home with you.

meals.breakfast: Resort farewell breakfast — full Japanese spread with seasonal fruit, grilled fish, miso, and premium coffee (¥5,000–¥8,000 per person or included)
meals.lunch: Airport premium dining — Narita's Nadaman (Japanese cuisine) or Haneda's Kokusai-Kanko Kaikan restaurant (¥4,000–¥8,000 per person)
meals.dinner: Onboard premium/business class dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for international flights to process tax-free refunds (bring all receipts and original passports), complete duty-free shopping, and clear security. Request a late check-out from the resort if the flight is in the evening. Arrange private airport transfer the night before for a stress-free departure morning.
